correctness.rationale: The independently randomized normal avoids angular orientation bias. Spherical Blaschke–Petkantschin yields the 3/4(1-h²) height weight and the area-biased angle density with E(T)=3/(2π); transforming the fourth point to signed volume cancels the factors and gives the exact constant 3πt. Boundary rejection sets have an integrable square-root profile. Circular Dyson integral at parameter -1/4 evaluates E(T^-1/2)=2Γ(1/4)/Γ(3/4)^3; dominated convergence establishes the sharp TV √t correction and scalar t^(3/2) term. All key steps are in RESULT.md. Standalone simulation and integration sanity checks pass, not serving as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Beyond the earlier unmarked conditional weak-limit theorem, the exact all-t marked rejection law provides an efficient sampler with acceptance tending to one versus naive O(t) rare-event acceptance, and gives an asymptotically independent rescaled signed-volume mark. The sharp explicit √t total-variation correction quantitatively bounds the entire marked approximation, not just pointwise or weak convergence; its nonanalytic boundary layer is a substantive structural quantitative law, not a routine renaming of the known leading limit.
